verdict_reason: All four emitted statistics are now exact, and I re-measured every one. hubness_k*_top1pct is the fix: it takes exactly the m = ceil(0.01 n) largest occurrence counts via np.partition, and I confirmed it equals a sorted-descending reference to the bit on real tables and on synthetic ones (Poisson(10), n=1e5: new 0.01937950 vs exact 0.01937950, where the old percentile form gave 0.02563114, +32.3%, selecting 1347 points instead of 1000). Degenerate anchor: 100 identical counts now return 0.010000 where the old form returned 1.000000. Real tables (k=10): gpt2 0.278447 vs old 0.280582 (540 selected instead of 503, +0.77%), pythia-70m 0.033039 vs 0.038327 (599 vs 504, +16.00%), pythia-160m 0.032864 vs 0.038319 (602 vs 504, +16.60%), distilgpt2 0.219739 vs 0.223678 (569 vs 503, +1.79%). The boundary tie is value-deterministic because the multiset of the m largest values is unique. S_Nk still matches scipy.stats.skew on the same occurrence vectors to exactly 0.0e+00 on all four real models, and the Gini rank form matches the O(n^2) pairwise-difference definition to 3.3e-16.
comparable_reason: Unchanged in kind by the fix, but its size moved on the two Pythia models, where top1pct fell 16%. Over the 61 archived models (d 512-7168, L 6-64, V 32k-262k) the associations are real but moderate and not arithmetic: k10_gini rho -0.432 (d_model), -0.260 (n_layers), +0.342 (vocab); k10_skew -0.266 / -0.094 / +0.201; k10_top1pct -0.341 / -0.150 / +0.267; k10_max -0.316 / -0.147 / +0.316. The observed spread is far larger than any size term (k10_skew 0.897 to 70.9 archived; on the four models I re-ran locally, k10_skew 1.119 (pythia-70m) to 34.023 (distilgpt2) at essentially identical vocabulary, 50304 vs 50257, which by itself refutes a vocabulary readout). Two standing caveats: hubness_k*_max is a raw extreme-value statistic whose sampling distribution depends on |V| and k with no size-matched null, and the geometry is hard-coded to cosine while the source paper's own anchors are Euclidean, so the shipped configuration cannot be validated against them.
github_repo: VarIr/scikit-hubness (no code was released with Radovanovic et al. 2010 or Tomasev et al. 2014)
github_reason: No code accompanies Radovanovic et al. 2010 or Tomasev et al. 2014 -- the JMLR page offers only [abs] [pdf] [bib] and the one URL in the body is a data source; OFAI/hub-toolbox, Hub Miner and scikit-hubness are all later independent works. I therefore re-ran scikit-hubness's kernel (k_occurrence = np.bincount(neigh_ind.ravel()) with self-hits filtered; k_skewness = scipy.stats.skew(k_occurrence); Gini = sum_ij|x_i-x_j|/(2 n sum x)) against BLME. On the occurrence vectors of the four real embedding tables the skew difference is exactly 0.0e+00 on all four; on synthetic Pareto counts the Gini difference is 3.3e-16. BLME's top1pct now also matches an exact sorted-descending top-m reference to the bit, a quantity scikit-hubness does not expose. Two deliberate BLME deviations remain: an all-tied vector returns 0.0 (scipy returns nan), and scikit-hubness's shuffle_equal=True tie randomisation is not implemented -- BLME breaks ties by torch.topk index order. PARTIAL: third-party reference, not the original authors' code.
paper_reason: Radovanovic et al. 2010 footnote 5 (p. 2492) publishes S_N5 for n=10000 iid data under EUCLIDEAN distance. I re-ran BLME's occurrence->skew kernel with Euclidean kNN over 5 fresh seeds per condition: uniform d=20 1.5524 +/- 0.0530 vs published 1.541 (+0.7%); uniform d=100 5.5055 +/- 1.0034 vs 5.445 (+1.1%); normal d=20 2.1036 +/- 0.0799 vs 2.055 (+2.4%). The two d=3 anchors are near-zero quantities and reproduce only in magnitude (uniform 0.1673 +/- 0.0322 vs 0.121; normal 0.0917 +/- 0.0200 vs 0.118). normal d=100 does NOT reproduce: I get 10.6103 +/- 3.3302 against a published 19.210, i.e. 2.6 sigma above my mean for a single-realisation statistic, so it should not be used as a parity target. All six anchors are Euclidean while BLME hard-codes cosine and exposes no switch, so they validate the kernel but not the shipped configuration.
confounds_reason: Unchanged by the fix in direction, though the pythia top1pct values moved 16%. On the 61-model archive the vocab associations are significant but modest (rho +0.20 to +0.34 across the six outputs) and the width associations are negative (rho -0.07 to -0.43), i.e. wider models are LESS hubby -- not the sign an arithmetic size readout would give. My own strongest control is the pair distilgpt2 (V=50257, k10_skew 34.023, gini 0.509, top1pct 0.220) against pythia-70m (V=50304, k10_skew 1.119, gini 0.319, top1pct 0.033): near-identical vocabulary, a 30x difference in skew. I do NOT reproduce the prior codex verdict of CONFIRMED. It still needs residualising on vocab_size before hubness_k10_gini is used as beyond-scale evidence.
defects: CODE: ties are still broken by torch.topk's index order rather than scikit-hubness's shuffle_equal=True default. Inert on the four real tables I checked (no exact cosine ties) but a latent trap for models with untrained or padded vocabulary slots initialised to a constant.

CONFIG/CODE: the distance metric is hard-coded to cosine (hubness.py:107) with no config switch, while the source paper treats the metric as part of the definition and every published S_Nk anchor I reproduced (uniform d=20 +0.7%, uniform d=100 +1.1%, normal d=20 +2.4%) is Euclidean.
CODE: hubness_k*_max is a raw extreme-value statistic exposed with no size-matched random-kNN null, so it cannot be read against its own baseline across models with different |V|.

SCOPE: the task measures the static INPUT EMBEDDING table (common.get_embeddings), not any hidden-state geometry. The class docstring is accurate, but study prose must not let hubness_k10_gini be read as a representation-level property.

PROVENANCE: task_metadata cites 'Radovanovic et al. 2010 (JMLR 11)'. For anyone writing this up: the S_Nk definition is an unnumbered display on p. 2492, not an equation number, and the anchors are in footnote 5. Note also that the published normal d=100 value 19.210 is not reproducible (I measure 10.61 +/- 3.33 over 5 seeds).
ANALYSIS DEBT: top1pct changed by up to +16.6% on shipped models, so any stored hubness_k*_top1pct column in the results archive predates the fix and must be recomputed rather than reused.
fix: The top1pct defect is closed; nothing further is required for correctness. Remaining: expose the distance metric as config and document that the published S_N5 anchors are Euclidean (and that normal d=100 = 19.210 is not a valid parity target -- I measure 10.61 +/- 3.33). Add seeded tie randomisation to match scikit-hubness's shuffle_equal. Emit a size-matched random-embedding null alongside skew and max. Recompute the archived hubness_k*_top1pct columns, which moved +16.0% (pythia-70m) and +16.6% (pythia-160m). Residualise on vocab_size before hubness_k10_gini is used as beyond-scale evidence.
